A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hepatic blood flow is controlled by the sympathetic nerves, and the hepatic arterial and the portal venous blood flow are regulated separately.
the liver blood volume is regulated by a combination of reflex mechanisms, the relative contributions of which depend upon the level of sinus pressure.
the hepatic nerves have a major role in regulating liver blood volume.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to change blood flow to the liver by stimulating the hepatic nerve.
it is important to consider the effect of the blood volume on the blood volume.
the liver is an important reservoir of blood that can be mobilized by reflex mechanisms that are activated by changes in blood pressure and by sympathetic nerve stimulation.
